public_rationale: The claim requires more than showing that left-handed drawing images exist. Marcus says a quick Google Images search supplies many examples and uses this to dismiss an objection about the system's training. The searches did not locate independent records of the relevant Google results or evidence establishing the system's exposure to the relevant information. Public discoverability would not by itself establish that exposure. Neither component is settled by the retrieved, citable evidence, so the whole claim remains unresolved.
limitations: Historical search results were not recovered; present-day results cannot establish the claimed experience in February 2024.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The critic's objection that the system had not been taught relevant information about left-handed drawing is nonsense, because a few seconds on Google Images turns up lots of people drawing with their left hand.
conditions: rebuttal to one critic's objection about the system

statement.excerpt: But this is nonsense; even a few seconds with Google Images supplies lots of people drawing with their left hand.
statement.document_title: Statistics versus Understanding: The Essence of What Ails Generative AI

from_speaker: the system had not been taught relevant information
even a few seconds with Google Images
lots of people drawing with their left hand
our_interpretation: The claim combines a factual premise about readily discoverable images with a rebuttal to the objection about the system's training. Support requires evidence for both.
I read 'a few seconds' as a quick, ordinary search, and 'lots' as numerous distinct examples readily visible without extended searching. Marcus supplies no exact time or count.
The relevant images must depict people drawing with their own left hand, rather than merely depict drawings of hands.

The rebuttal requires evidence that the system had received relevant information about left-handed drawing. It does not require proof that every Google result was included in training, or that the system reliably understood handedness.
The immediate context describes a search possible at publication. I therefore use February 13, 2024 as the target date.
The description of a critic's objection supplies argumentative context, not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous search records or a credible historical reconstruction show numerous distinct images of people drawing with their left hand readily discoverable through an ordinary Google Images search on the target date. Evidence about the system's actual training also establishes that it received relevant information about left-handed drawing, defeating the objection as Marcus describes it. Public availability alone does not satisfy this second requirement.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable historical search evidence shows that ordinary relevant Google Images searches did not readily return numerous such examples, or reliable evidence about the identified system establishes that it had not received the relevant information. Missing search archives or undisclosed training data alone do not establish contradiction.
